title: In Vitro Lipid-Protein Interactions Using Liposome Flotation Assay
author: Khadayat, House, et al.
materials: Round Bottom Disposable Borosilicate Glass Tubes

steps.title: Measure liposome size by DLS
steps.instruction: Transfer 100 µL of the liposome suspension into a DLS cuvette; use liposome buffer without liposomes as the blank control; run the DLS instrument with the DYNAMICS program to record liposome diameter and polydispersity; note that PC/PE liposomes average 67.697 nm, PC/PE/PA liposomes average 68.453 nm, and buffer‑only shows no liposomes.

substeps.instruction: Prepare blank cuvette with liposome buffer only.
Load 100 µL liposome sample into cuvette.
Measure using DLS (DYNAMICS program).
Record diameter and polydispersity values.

steps.title: Incubate protein with liposomes
steps.instruction: Add purified protein to a final concentration of 4 µM and extruded liposomes to a final concentration of 2 mM in a total volume of 60 µL liposome buffer in an Eppendorf tube; also prepare a negative control containing 4 µM protein in 60 µL buffer without liposomes; incubate both mixtures at 20 °C for 1 hour while gently rocking.

substeps.instruction: Mix protein (4 µM) and liposomes (2 mM) to 60 µL total.
Prepare control: protein (4 µM) in 60 µL buffer, no liposomes.
Incubate at 20 °C for 1 h with gentle rocking.

steps.title: Prepare sucrose gradient
steps.instruction: During the incubation, prepare 60 %, 20 %, and 10 % (w/v) sucrose solutions in liposome buffer; after incubation, transfer the 60 µL liposome‑protein mixture to the bottom of a polycarbonate centrifuge tube, add 60 µL of the 60 % sucrose solution to obtain a 30 % sucrose‑liposome‑protein layer and mix gently; then carefully layer 240 µL of 20 % sucrose, followed by 240 µL of 10 % sucrose, and finally 120 µL of liposome buffer on top without mixing, using the tube wall to avoid disturbing the layers. (Nycodenz can be used as an alternative to sucrose.)

substeps.instruction: Make 60 % (w/v) sucrose in liposome buffer.
Make 20 % (w/v) sucrose in liposome buffer.
Make 10 % (w/v) sucrose in liposome buffer.
Transfer 60 µL liposome‑protein mixture to bottom of polycarbonate tube.
Add 60 µL 60 % sucrose (creates 30 % sucrose layer) and mix gently.
Layer 240 µL 20 % sucrose on top, do not mix.
Layer 240 µL 10 % sucrose on top, do not mix.
Layer 120 µL liposome buffer on top, do not mix.

steps.title: Collect fractions and add SDS buffer
steps.instruction: After centrifugation (not detailed), collect twelve 60 µL fractions from top to bottom of the gradient; mix each fraction with an appropriate amount of SDS sample buffer; load the fractions sequentially onto an SDS‑PAGE gel.

substeps.instruction: Collect 12 fractions (60 µL each) from the gradient.
Add suitable volume of SDS sample buffer to each fraction.
Load fractions sequentially into SDS‑PAGE gel.

steps.title: Immunoblot fractions
steps.instruction: Perform standard immunoblotting: transfer proteins from the gel to a membrane, probe with a primary antibody reactive with the protein of interest (e.g., anti‑6×His), apply a compatible secondary antibody (e.g., IR‑conjugated for LI‑COR), and scan the blot with an imaging system suitable for the secondary antibody.

substeps.instruction: Transfer proteins to membrane.
Block membrane (standard blocking buffer).
Incubate with primary antibody (e.g., anti‑6×His).
Wash membrane.
Incubate with appropriate secondary antibody (e.g., IR‑conjugated).
Wash and scan with compatible imaging system.

steps.title: Analyze blot for interaction
steps.instruction: Examine the scanned images; protein bands appearing in the top fractions indicate lipid‑protein interaction, whereas the negative‑control blot should show protein only in the bottom fractions. Interpret the pattern accordingly.
